info.title: Java Backend Challenge API
info.description: Sports training scheduling and registration API. All eight operations are implemented. Coach names retain the public name field and normalize ASCII whitespace. Timestamps require an explicit offset, are truncated to microseconds and return UTC. Errors use application/json with stable codes and optional fieldErrors. See README.md for setup and a complete HTTP walkthrough, and documentation/ADR-001-coach-name-expansion.md for database compatibility and rollback decisions.

servers.description: Local service; runtime Swagger documents implemented endpoints.

post.description: Name and email must be nonblank; email must be valid. Emails are not unique identities. Normalize surrounding and repeated ASCII whitespace (space, tab, line breaks, vertical tab and form feed) in coach names. Internally store the first word as first_name and the remainder as last_name; a single word has an empty last_name. Return the same id/name/email DTO with the normalized public name. Participant names remain unchanged. Reject an existing name/email combination within this role with 409 DUPLICATE_COACH. Compare case-insensitively, normalize ASCII whitespace in names and trim surrounding ASCII whitespace from emails, preserving accents and existing public values. The Java service checks existence before saving; simultaneous duplicate creations are not prevented.

post.description: Validate input, then coach existence, then overlap. Normalize timestamps to microsecond precision before comparing or storing. For the same coach, overlap is existing.start < proposed.end AND proposed.start < existing.end. Adjacent intervals are allowed; different coaches may share an interval. Serialize check/insert in one transaction by locking the coach row through commit, including an initially empty schedule.

get.description: Optional coachId/from/to filters combine with AND. Supplied bounds are normalized to microsecond precision. Select interval intersections: endTime > from and startTime < to. Either bound may be omitted. Reject from >= to after normalization. Order by startTime then UUID. No matches, including an unknown coach filter, return empty content and zero totals. Query parameters use standard Spring conversion; empty values are treated as omitted. URL-encode positive offsets so + is not decoded as a space. Returns {content,page,size,totalElements,totalPages}. Pages beyond the last return empty content with matching totals. Invalid pagination returns 400 before resource lookup.

delete.description: Check session existence first. Block while any registrations exist with SESSION_HAS_REGISTRATIONS. In one transaction, execute a delete by ID and inspect its affected row count; zero rows return SESSION_NOT_FOUND. Translate only a violation of fk_registrations_session into SESSION_HAS_REGISTRATIONS if a registration appears after the check. After cancellation of all registrations, deletion succeeds. Repeated deletion returns 404. Keep coaches and participants.

value.title: Conflict
value.detail: Cancel all registrations before deleting this session.

post.description: Validate input, then lock the session row, then check participant existence, duplicate and capacity in one transaction. Duplicate takes precedence over full. The last available slot succeeds. Flush the insert before returning the generated registration ID; translate only a violation of uq_registrations_session_participant to DUPLICATE_REGISTRATION. Other unexpected persistence failures remain sanitized INTERNAL_ERROR responses. Hold the session lock through commit or rollback to prevent concurrent overbooking under READ COMMITTED. Different sessions lock independently. Concurrent last-slot requests return one 201 and one 409 SESSION_FULL; duplicate requests retain DUPLICATE_REGISTRATION precedence.

get.description: Include participant id, name, email and registrationId for discoverable cancellation. Order by participant id. An existing empty session returns empty content and zero totals; a missing session returns 404. One read-only transaction checks existence then fetches registrations with participants through an EntityGraph, avoiding per-participant queries. Returns {content,page,size,totalElements,totalPages}. Pages beyond the last return empty content with matching totals. Invalid pagination returns 400 before resource lookup.

delete.description: Check session existence, then execute a single delete scoped by sessionId and registrationId in one transaction. Missing registration or one belonging to another session returns 404. Delete only the relationship, freeing capacity; registering again creates a new ID. Repeated cancellation returns 404. Preserve participants and other registrations.

name.description: Required nonblank name. ASCII whitespace is normalized; for example, "  Alex   Rivera  " returns "Alex Rivera".
Coach name with surrounding and repeated ASCII whitespace normalized to single spaces. Public field remains unchanged during internal name expansion.

x-decisions.architecture: One application and one database; feature-oriented packages, controllers, application services, repositories, entities and DTOs. Do not expose JPA entities. Avoid unnecessary abstraction.
x-decisions.stack: Java 21, Spring Boot 3.5.16, Maven 3.9.16 with Wrapper 3.3.4, Spring Web, Bean Validation, Spring Data JPA, PostgreSQL, Flyway, JUnit, Testcontainers and springdoc 2.9.1. Other dependency and plugin versions are managed by the Boot parent.
x-decisions.schemaOwnership: Flyway owns the schema; Hibernate ddl-auto=validate, never update. Released migrations remain unchanged.
x-decisions.time: Persist timestamptz; compare Java Instant values in UTC; configure UTC. Input timestamps must be ISO-8601 strings with explicit offsets; reject numeric timestamps. Truncate to microsecond precision before window validation, overlap checks and persistence; responses use the same precision in UTC Z. Original input timezone is not retained.
x-decisions.identity: UUID IDs, including registration IDs. Names and emails individually are not unique; reject matching name/email combinations separately within coaches and participants. The same combination can belong to both roles.
x-decisions.validation: Nonblank names, location and valid nonblank emails, capacity > 0, startTime < endTime; past sessions allowed. Invalid UUIDs and offset-free timestamps return 400.
x-decisions.publicCoachName: Keep the name API field through internal first_name/last_name expansion.
x-decisions.nameSplit: For coaches, normalize ASCII whitespace identically in Java and SQL (space, tab, LF, VT, FF, CR), trim surrounding spaces, first word -> first_name, remainder -> last_name; a single word has empty last_name. Keep the public name API field, recomposed from split fields. Names are normalized at creation, legacy writes and backfill. This is a pragmatic, culturally imperfect policy; participants are unchanged.
x-decisions.migrationCompatibility: V3 retains legacy name, backfills canonical names and first_name/last_name without changing IDs, emails or relations, then requires non-null split fields. A BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger handles legacy-only and split-only writes. Detect actual UPDATE changes with IS DISTINCT FROM; if both representations are supplied/changed, require equality after normalization or reject with SQLSTATE 23514. Split writers provide both fields, including empty last_name for single names; nulls remain invalid. Canonicalize the composed full name and split by first word. Email-only updates leave names untouched. Old readers continue using name; new JPA maps only split fields. Keep V3 when rolling back the application. Defer dropping name/compatibility triggers until old versions and rollback dependencies retire. V1/V2 remain immutable.
x-decisions.errors: Spring MVC errors use application/problem+json with type=about:blank, standard HTTP title, matching status, safe detail, request-path instance without query, stable code and optional sorted/deduplicated fieldErrors for body validation. Top-level message is removed; fieldErrors retains {field,message}. Unexpected 500 errors are generic; internal details stay in server logs.
x-decisions.documentation: Version README.md at the repository root and documentation/ADR-001-coach-name-expansion.md as the reviewer guide and migration ADR. Keep all docs/ contents, including working memories and ticket notes, ignored.
x-decisions.git: Branch exactly ticket ID; Conventional Commits include ticket ID. Commit locally only; owner performs push. No PR creation or remote operations in JBC-001.
x-decisions.testing: Prioritize business logic and HTTP integration tests backed by PostgreSQL. No dedicated Flyway or migration-only tests, per owner scope adjustment in JBC-004. Flyway continues to apply and validate migrations on normal application startup.
x-decisions.localRuntime: docker compose up --build builds the JAR inside a Java 21 builder and starts a non-root Java 21 runtime with PostgreSQL. GET /actuator/health returns 200 with status UP once the application and database are healthy. PostgreSQL data is stored in a named volume.
x-decisions.ci: PRs targeting main and pushes to main run Maven verify with Java 21 and PostgreSQL Testcontainers on Ubuntu 24.04. Cache only dependencies; never skip tests. Upload Surefire/Failsafe reports on failure. Require the Maven verify status check in main protection to enforce the merge gate; workflow alone does not enforce it.
x-decisions.schedulingConcurrency: Within one transaction, lock the coach row with PESSIMISTIC_WRITE before checking existing.start < proposed.end AND existing.end > proposed.start and inserting the session. The lock also covers empty schedules and is held through commit. Every session creation uses this path; direct database writes bypass this application guarantee. Different coaches lock different rows.
x-decisions.sessionFiltering: Optional coachId/from/to combine with AND. Match endTime > from and startTime < to for supplied bounds, after truncating bounds to microseconds. Either bound may be omitted; from >= to returns 400. Unknown coaches match no sessions. Empty query parameter values follow standard Spring conversion and are treated as omitted. Sort by startTime then UUID; paginated content with totals. One content query fetches sessions and coaches, with a count query when needed; no resource-existence lookup is needed.
x-decisions.registrationCreation: One transaction locks the session row with PESSIMISTIC_WRITE, checks participant, duplicate and capacity in that order, then saveAndFlush returns the generated registration ID. Duplicate takes precedence even when full. Translate only the named uq_registrations_session_participant constraint violation to DUPLICATE_REGISTRATION and roll back; unrelated failures use the sanitized generic 500 handler. The lock is retained through commit or rollback, serializing registration creation per session under PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED, including across application instances. Different sessions lock independently. The V2 unique constraint still prevents duplicate pairs. Direct SQL writes bypass the application capacity guarantee; a concurrent cancellation may free capacity after a SESSION_FULL response. No schema change is needed.
x-decisions.registrationLifecycle: Participant listing returns id/name/email/registrationId ordered by participant UUID, in paginated content with totals, with empty content for existing empty sessions and 404 for missing sessions. Fetch participants with registrations. Cancellation checks session first and atomically deletes only the matching session/registration pair; zero affected rows mean REGISTRATION_NOT_FOUND. Repeated cancellation is 404; capacity is freed and reinscription generates a new ID. Session deletion checks existence then registrations, rejects nonempty sessions with SESSION_HAS_REGISTRATIONS, and deletes by ID with row-count checking. Only fk_registrations_session violations are mapped to that conflict. Preserve coaches, participants and all unrelated registrations. No cascading deletion, migration or concurrency capacity change.
x-decisions.pagination: Both listing endpoints accept page (default 0, minimum 0) and size (default 20, range 1–100). Empty values use defaults. Return {content,page,size,totalElements,totalPages}; retain fixed ordering and filter before pagination/counting. Invalid values return 400 before existence checks. Out-of-range pages retain totals with empty content. This replaces the baseline array responses.
x-decisions.peopleCreation: After HTTP validation, the Java service checks normalized name/email existence before saving in its transaction. Repository EXISTS queries normalize both stored values and parameters: lower(normalize_coach_name(name)), and lower(email trimmed of surrounding space/TAB/LF/VT/FF/CR). Names collapse the same six ASCII whitespace characters; accents remain significant. Preserve current public values and validation. Return 409 DUPLICATE_COACH or DUPLICATE_PARTICIPANT. Existing duplicates are not deleted or merged. No UNIQUE, migration or extra lock is added; simultaneous creations can both pass the check. This is an additional owner-selected business rule rather than a PDF requirement.
